extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in digital identity, NGOs, and ID2020
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia encyclopedia entry summarizing the nonprofit ID2020: its formation, mission, participants, activities, and the misinformation/conspiracy theories surrounding it. Not a how-to or guideline document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide legal identity for all (UN SDG 2030)
rubrics_metrics.description: ID2020 is a public-private consortium in service of the United Nations 2030 Sustainable Development Goal of providing legal identity for all people, including the world's most vulnerable populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the organization's high-level mission; tied to the UN 2030 agenda and efforts to reach people living without recognized identification (cited figure: 1.5 billion). Not a procedural checklist but a stated goal framing the NGO's activities and partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten-point mission statement (including user control over identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: ID2020 has published a ten-point mission statement, which includes: "We believe that individuals must have control over their own digital identities, including how personal data is collected, used, and shared."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mission point functions as a normative principle guiding program design and partnerships (emphasis on user control, privacy and data governance). The article does not reproduce the full ten points but highlights this principle as central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining what constitutes a "good" digital ID
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2018 summit focused on defining what constitutes a "good" digital ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summit participation included experts in blockchain and cryptographic technology and representatives of technical standards bodies to identify how technology and private-sector expertise could achieve the digital identity goal. The article mentions sponsors and partners (UN agencies, tech firms, foundations) as context for these discussions, but does not list explicit criteria of a 'good' digital ID on the page.
